normalized_issues.title: Path traversal protection ignores the `addinSessionId` path segment

merged_from.title: Path traversal protection ignores the `addinSessionId` path segment
Screenshot endpoint validates only filename, leaving addinSessionId as an unchecked path segment

normalized_issues.core_problem: The screenshot endpoint `GET /screenshots/{addinSessionId}/{filename}` applies path-traversal guards only to `filename`. The `addinSessionId` segment is inserted into the filesystem path without format validation or canonical-path verification, enabling escape from `ScreenshotRootPath` or cross-session file access.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 9: "Path traversal guards: reject any filename containing `..`, `/`, `\`, or null bytes." — no equivalent guard is specified for `addinSessionId`.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Constrain `addinSessionId` to a strict UUID format (regex or `Guid.TryParse`), build the full resolved path canonically (`Path.GetFullPath`), and reject any resolved path that does not start with the canonical `ScreenshotRootPath`.

normalized_issues.title: GET / does not define how the 'selected session' is chosen

merged_from.title: GET / does not define how the "selected session" is chosen
GET / depends on an undefined session-selection contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: The mandatory timeline page populates `TimelineViewModel` via `ListEntriesAsync` for 'the selected session', but the spec never defines how a session is selected, what the default is when multiple sessions exist, how a user switches sessions, or what the empty-state behavior is.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 4.1: "The `TimelineViewModel` is populated at page-render time via `IDhfRepository.ListSessionsAsync` and `IDhfRepository.ListEntriesAsync` for the selected session."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define the selection contract explicitly: e.g. `GET /?sessionId={uuid}` with a documented default rule (most recent session) when `sessionId` is absent, plus defined behavior for missing/invalid IDs and the no-sessions empty state.

normalized_issues.title: Integrity endpoint timeout/truncation behavior is absent from the API contract

merged_from.title: Deep integrity timeout behavior is specified but missing from the API contract
Integrity endpoint timeout behavior is not represented in its API contract
Deep validation can still produce unbounded HTTP request hangs

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 13 states the endpoint returns partial results with a 'truncation flag' on timeout, but the Section 5.3 response schema contains no such field. No concrete timeout value, cancellation-token propagation, or max-duration guard is specified. Clients cannot distinguish a complete validation from a timed-out partial result.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 13: "The endpoint returns what's been validated so far with a truncation flag." Section 5.3 response schema: only `sessionId`, `mode`, `valid`, `entriesChecked`, `failures`, `warnings` — no truncation field.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add explicit fields to the integrity response schema: `truncated` (bool), `timeoutMs` (int), `lastSequenceChecked` (int). Define semantics for `valid` when `truncated=true`. Specify a hard timeout (e.g. 8 seconds) with `CancellationToken` propagation, or make deep validation an async background job returning a `jobId`.

normalized_issues.title: Repository failure handling contradicts Postgres-unreachable handling

merged_from.title: Repository failure handling conflicts with unreachable-Postgres behavior

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 13 assigns HTTP 500 to `IDhfRepository` throws and HTTP 503 to Postgres-unreachable, but a Postgres outage surfaces as an `IDhfRepository` exception. The spec provides no exception taxonomy or result contract to distinguish the two cases, leading to inconsistent status codes and undefined banner-trigger logic for the HTML route.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 13: "**IDhfRepository throws:** The endpoint returns 500..." and "**Postgres is unreachable:** ... The JSON endpoints return 503."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define an exception taxonomy: e.g. `RepositoryUnavailableException` (connection/timeout) → 503 + degraded-page banner; all other repository exceptions → 500. Specify how Razor page routes catch and render the banner vs. error state.

normalized_issues.title: ACC-08 performance acceptance criterion is not reproducibly testable

merged_from.title: ACC-08 performance is not reproducible or CI-testable as written
ACC-08 performance testing is not reproducible as an automated test

normalized_issues.core_problem: The 1-second render threshold is tied to a specific machine (GE75) with unspecified cache state, dataset characteristics, and measurement boundaries. The automated test is otherwise described as portable and in-process, making CI results hardware-dependent and non-deterministic.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 4.1: "Must render within 1 second for a 20-entry session on the demo laptop (GE75)." Section 10: "`TimelinePerformanceTests` — ACC-08; 20-entry session renders within 1s on representative hardware (integration test)"
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either move ACC-08 to a manual demo-validation procedure with the GE75 threshold, or define a reproducible benchmark harness with fixed dataset, explicit measurement start/stop points, warmup passes, and a hardware-agnostic target (e.g. p95 latency under controlled load).

normalized_issues.title: Read-only guarantee is not enforced at the dependency boundary

merged_from.title: The read-only guarantee is not enforced at the actual dependency boundary

normalized_issues.core_problem: The architecture test only scans Viewer-namespace source for SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE strings. This does not prevent the viewer from invoking write-capable repository methods or receiving a write-capable `IDhfRepository` implementation. The stated strong non-write guarantee lacks an enforcement mechanism.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-06-003: "Architecture test (`ViewerReadOnlyArchitectureTests`) asserts no SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in any Viewer namespace." — scanning strings in one namespace does not constrain injected dependencies.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Introduce a `IReadOnlyDhfRepository` interface exposing only read methods, inject only that interface into the viewer, and add a test that fails if any write-capable type is resolvable from the viewer's DI container.

normalized_issues.title: Entry detail JSON schema is unspecified

merged_from.title: Entry detail JSON schema is unspecified

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 5.2 references `ToolCallRow[]` and `DecorationRow[]` in the response but defines no fields, types, nullability, ordering guarantees, or nested object shapes. The entry-detail page and its tests cannot be built without inventing a private schema.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.2: "Full JSON detail including `ToolCallRow[]` and `DecorationRow[]`. Used by the entry detail page."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a complete JSON contract for `/api/dhf/entries/{entryId}` covering every field name, type, enum domain, nullability, ordering, and screenshot URL representation.

normalized_issues.title: Read consistency is undefined during concurrent orchestrator writes

merged_from.title: Read consistency is undefined while the orchestrator is actively appending entries

normalized_issues.core_problem: The viewer runs in-process with the orchestrator. `GET /` issues separate `ListSessionsAsync` and `ListEntriesAsync` calls; `app.js` polls every 3 seconds; integrity validation reads live session data. No snapshot isolation, transaction boundaries, or concurrent-write behavior is defined, risking internally inconsistent counts, timelines, or false tamper reports.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Sections 3, 4.1, 7, SDR-06-005: viewer runs in-process; separate repository calls; 3-second polling; shallow validation on page render.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define repository read-isolation requirements for viewer endpoints (e.g. repeatable-read snapshot), or explicitly restrict integrity validation and timeline counts to closed/stable sessions.

normalized_issues.title: `screenshotRootPath` startup validation is internally inconsistent
normalized_issues.core_problem: `ViewerOptions.ScreenshotRootPath` is modeled as a non-nullable required property (`default!`), but the startup-failure rule is conditional on stretch endpoints being enabled. The spec does not define what happens when stretch endpoints are disabled and the path is absent or invalid.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 3: `public string ScreenshotRootPath { get; init; } = default!;` Section 12: "The viewer will throw at startup if `screenshotRootPath` doesn't exist (stretch endpoints only — mandatory endpoints don't need it)."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Make `ScreenshotRootPath` nullable or optional; validate it only when `EnableStretchEndpoints=true`; document both branches explicitly.

normalized_issues.title: Integrity validity semantics are undefined when screenshot files are missing

merged_from.title: Integrity validity is undefined when screenshot files are missing

normalized_issues.core_problem: The sample integrity response shows `"valid": true` alongside a `screenshot_file_missing` warning. The spec never defines whether missing screenshots constitute a failure (changing `valid` to false), a warning only, or are conditional on ledger metadata.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.3 sample response: `"valid": true` with warning `{ "reason": "screenshot_file_missing" }`.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define an explicit taxonomy of conditions that are `failures` (set `valid=false`) vs. `warnings` (leave `valid=true`), and document the rule for screenshot-missing specifically.

normalized_issues.title: Mandatory/stretch split is undermined by the project scaffold and test inventory

merged_from.title: Project shape and test list already embed stretch features, undermining mandatory/stretch split

normalized_issues.core_problem: The project layout, class names, and test list already fully scaffold stretch features (EntryDetailEndpoints.cs, IntegrityEndpoints.cs, ExportEndpoints.cs, EntryDetail.cshtml, PdfExportTests, ScreenshotPathTraversalTests), defeating the stated baseline-only intent of SDR-06-004.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 1 project shape lists all stretch files; Section 10 test list includes PdfExportTests and ScreenshotPathTraversalTests without gating.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Provide a minimal mandatory project shape separately, and move stretch scaffolding and tests into a clearly gated appendix or follow-on spec section.

normalized_issues.title: Localhost-only threat model lacks pluggable auth and boundary enumeration

merged_from.title: Localhost-only threat model brittle against real-world exposure vectors

normalized_issues.core_problem: The spec relies on process isolation with no auth, no rate limiting, and no logging, while exposing full design history and a filesystem-derived screenshot endpoint. Common vectors (ngrok, Docker port mapping, reverse proxies, shared dev machines) are not addressed, and retrofitting auth later cascades into every endpoint.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-06-002: "Binds to `http://127.0.0.1:7879`. No auth. Hackathon scope."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Design endpoints with a pluggable auth middleware stub (even if disabled by flag for hackathon). Explicitly enumerate and document the boundary conditions under which the 7879 surface is considered safe.

normalized_issues.title: 3-second polling chosen over lighter real-time alternatives without adequate justification

merged_from.title: Rejection of real-time updates creates self-inflicted staleness and polling tax

normalized_issues.core_problem: The orchestrator already runs a real-time bridge on :7878. The viewer deliberately uses 3-second polling, guaranteeing up-to-3-second UI lag during active modeling sessions. The stated rationale ('no second WS endpoint') does not consider SSE, which is lighter and avoids a second WebSocket.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 7: "Specifically no WebSocket to the viewer — the existing WebSocket at :7878 is the add-in bridge, not a viewer push channel. Polling is sufficient for hackathon scope."
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Consider SSE as a lighter alternative to polling. If polling is retained, document the latency trade-off explicitly and confirm it is acceptable for the demo use case.

dropped_findings.title: Stretch-enabled startup is not cross-platform or deterministic as specified
dropped_findings.reason: duplicate — the cross-platform path concern is substantially covered by R1-ISSUE-009 (screenshotRootPath startup validation inconsistency); the Windows-path-in-config observation is a style/config detail subsumed by that issue
